inputs.text: Health workers took their opposition to the proposed reform bills to Unity Fountain in Maitama on Thursday, and that protest should be heard as more than “union interests.” The people who keep a strained health sector running have a direct stake in whether reforms protect patients and working conditions—or deepen existing failures. The National Assembly should scrutinize the bills on their merits, but that means listening to frontline workers, not treating public pressure as a reason to dismiss them. Reform should strengthen care for everyone, especially those least able to absorb the cost of a broken system.
